title: Rated power and active time
hook: A 100 W fridge compressor runs a quarter of the time. Energy per day?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Use a stated duty fraction rather than treating rated power as continuous.

misconception: Every elapsed hour must be charged at full on-state power.
objective: Use a stated duty fraction rather than treating rated power as continuous.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Verified as a derivation from unit definitions, not on the cited energy.gov.au page (not opened). Energy (Wh) = power (W) × time (h), and 1 kWh = 1000 Wh, so kWh = W × h ÷ 1000 for a constant load; a per-kWh price is by definition charged per kWh, so energy cost = kWh × price, and any stated fixed charge is a separate term. Matches the stage formulas printed by resourceFormula (e.g. (100×0.25×8)÷1000 = 0.2 kWh).
